document.title: Working with agents
document.p: sxml is built by an orchestrator session that delegates packets to subagents. This directory holds the prompts those agents get, so the work can be picked up by any later session and is never stuck in one.

item.p: BRIEF.md: the common brief every agent follows.
PACKET.md: how to work a packet from docs/tasks/.
QUEUE.md: what runs now, what comes next, and the leftovers that no packet owns yet. The orchestrator keeps it current.

section.title: How a session continues the work

item.p: Read CLAUDE.md, then the queue (tools/spec/spec markdown agents/QUEUE) and the state of the packets (tools/spec/spec status).
Pick the next packets from the queue and tools/spec/spec status PHASE. Packets that own disjoint files may run at the same time.

Give each agent a prompt that says: read the brief and the packet guide (tools/spec/spec markdown agents/BRIEF, tools/spec/spec markdown agents/PACKET), the packet's number (tools/spec/spec brief N.M), the decisions to read first, the goal and its done-when, and which other packets run at the same time and the files they own.

When an agent reports, record what it left over in the queue (tools/spec/spec text agents/QUEUE#SECTION, edit, then tools/spec/spec amend agents/QUEUE#SECTION --body=-), and commit that change on its own.

section.p: The prompt of each packet is its article (tools/spec/spec brief N.M) plus the lines given in step 3; anything an agent decides goes into a decision and its commit messages, so the history explains itself.
